items.description: Vertical video. Police Week memorial footage: a CBP and Border Patrol honor guard folding a flag and a wreath and plaque presentation, with on-screen caption text ('FALLEN AGENTS,' 'OF THE FALLEN'). has_audio is false and there is no music track and no added stylization, so it is an event and ceremony recording with text overlays. | Each year, we come together, we take time out to honor our fallen agents, officers and our professional staff. We stand together with our law enforcement partners from around the nation as we honor Police Week, which honors our fallen officers across the entire nation that gave up their lives while protecting others. This observance that holds very deep meaning to CBP its employees, families and friends of the fallen. This specific ceremony serves as a solemn reminder of the brave men and women who gave their lives serving within CBP or as part of one of our legacy agencies. To all of our CBP families, we honor you and we grieve alongside you. You will forever be part of the CBP family.

THE BORDER IS CLOSED.
Border security, enforcement efforts, and prosecutions have increased, resulting in zero illegal immigrants being released at the southwest border over the past six months.
Illegal entry into this country will have consequences. https://t.co/UkZyVu9Fs4
items.description: A single static talking-head clip of a CBP Border Patrol agent in uniform speaking to camera against a flat green geometric backdrop, with burned-in caption subtitles, stating zero illegal immigrants were released at the southwest border in six months. There is no music. | The United States border patrols released zero illegal immigrants into this country in the last six months. And we don't plan on breaking that pattern, we're going to continue to release zero. And look, we've done that without a single change in law. And when people know that if they're across the border illegally, they're going to be apprehended, prosecuted, and returned back to their country, they stop coming. We're sending a clear message, the border's closed, you're not going to come into this country illegally. And if you do, you're going to be apprehended, you're going to be prosecuted and returned to your home country.

items.description: An ABC 'This Week' news broadcast clip of an anchor reporting on renewed scrutiny of Afghan vetting and the DC attack, with network chyrons. | If you remember during that operation, when Afghanistan was abandoned, people were just put on aircraft and brought to the United States. The administration said at that time that they would vet them when they got here. They did, but they didn't do a thorough investigation. What they did was check a few names and a few data points. What President Trump has put in place now for vetting is biometric information, checking social media platforms, communications, contacts, matching updates of service. That was never done under Joe Biden. He didn't do that. In fact, he brought people to this country and then just said, well, we'll vet them later. Okay. And that's how things like this happen. I mean, you remember, this individual's application to be in this country started under the administration of Joe Biden. The information was gathered under the administration of Joe Biden and the consequences of this horrific shooting and death of Sarah lays directly on the shoulders of Joe Biden and his administration.

Las Vegas police arrested John Young Cotter Johnstone, an illegal alien from the UK, who police say was captured on video dragging and swinging dogs by their leashes and kicking one dog.

Johnstone faces multiple charges connected to animal abuse he allegedly committed while working at a local rescue in Nevada.

The same day Johnstone was arrested, ICE issued an immigration detainer with the Clark County Detention Center. The next day, April 2, Clark County officials honored the detainer, and ICE took custody of the alleged animal abuser.

Johnstone came to the United States under the Visa Waiver Program as a visitor. He was supposed to leave the country by Feb. 22, 2022. 

ICE secured a final order of removal. He’ll stay in ICE detention pending local charges.

items.tweet_text: Remember to remain vigilant as you enjoy the summer weather. Report suspicious activity to local authorities while you’re out an about. #protectyoureveryday #seesay https://t.co/kB6XRDRPCF
items.description: Video. A 2018 DHS 'See Something, Say Something / Protect Your Every Day' public-service announcement. Everyday people, including a firefighter and a teacher in a classroom, deliver spoken testimonial lines to camera asking viewers to report suspicious activity. It ends on a See/Say end card with the DHS seal. The audio is spoken word, not a song. It is a conventional informational PSA from the first Trump term. | We're all part of your community. We all play a role in keeping our community safe, so protect there every day. If you see something suspicious, say something to local authorities. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: Together with the @NFL, we are working hard to protect fans. Keep an eye out while at the game and report suspicious activity to local authorities. #SeeSay #ProtectYourEveryDay https://t.co/xOQe7WYixt
items.description: Video. A 2018 DHS and NFL 'See Something, Say Something' public-service announcement. An NFL referee in a locker room delivers a spoken testimonial drawing an analogy between officiating and watching the stands, and asks fans to report suspicious activity. It closes on NFL and DHS logos and the line 'We care about the safety of our fans.' The audio is a spoken testimonial, not music. It is a conventional safety spot. | I pay attention for eleven. I watch plays and make important calls. While I'm busy watching the game, I need your help keeping an eye on the stands. We all play our role in protecting our communities. If you see something suspicious, make the right call. Tell alone for some official. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: We all have something worth protecting so if you see something, say something. Report suspicious activity to local law enforcement. #SeeSay #ProtectYourEveryDay https://t.co/0391dzsvai
items.description: Video. A 2018 DHS 'See Something, Say Something / Why I Say Something' public-service announcement. A young woman on a city bus and at a station delivers spoken testimonial lines about why she reports suspicious activity, with single-word text cues ('WHY') and a closing 'If you see something, say something' card with the DHS seal. The audio is a spoken testimonial, not music. | If you see something, why do you say something? I see safe from my friends. For much immunity. For everyone here, we all have something worth protecting, a why that unifies us. Reports of suspicious activity to local authorities. If you see something, say something. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: Why say something if you see something? #SeeSay to protect your family, friends and community; report suspicious activity to local authorities. #WhyISeeSay https://t.co/iaTmklE4da
items.description: Video. A 2018 DHS 'If You See Something, Say Something' counterterrorism PSA showing travelers at a hotel valet, a restaurant, and a family at an outdoor party, with a voiceover asking people to stay aware of their surroundings and report suspicious activity to local authorities. It is a narrated awareness spot with no music track. It predates the second Trump administration. | Travel is part of the American way of life. When we're on vacation, we keep an eye out for anything that looks out of place. Miss your bag. When we travel from city to city, we pay attention to our surroundings. Everyone plays a role in keeping our community safe. Whether you're traveling for business or pleasure, be aware of your surroundings. If you see something suspicious, say something to local authorities. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: Together with the @NFL, we are working hard to protect fans. Keep an eye out while at the game and report suspicious activity to local authorities. #SeeSay #ProtectYourEveryDay https://t.co/WfcLzdmj7W
items.description: Video. A 2018 DHS and NFL co-branded 'See Something, Say Something' announcement in which an NFL referee in a locker room speaks to camera, comparing officiating to watching the stands, and asks fans to report suspicious activity to local law enforcement. A single narrator speaks, with NFL and DHS logos and no music track. | I pay attention for eleven. I watch plays and make important calls. While I'm busy watching the game, I need your help keeping an eye on the stands. We all play our role in protecting our communities. If you see something suspicious, make the right call. Tell alone for some official. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: Take this #SeeSayChallenge and let us know how you did! Remember to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity to local authorities. #SeeSay https://t.co/Ea0PB25CR2
items.description: Video. A 2018 to 2019 DHS 'SeeSay Challenge' PSA. A host holds a 'How many times is...' cue card while people pass a yellow backpack around a college-style setting, an attention game asking viewers how observant they are. It ends with a card directing to DHS.gov/TheChallenge. It is a narrated interactive informational PSA. It predates the second Trump administration. | Here's your challenge. How many times is the yellow backpack passed? Go. How observant were you? Complete the challenge at dhs.gov slash the challenge. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: #ProtectYourEveryDay this week; make sure to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity to local authorities today and every day; by doing this, you're protecting your community. #SeeSay #protectyoureveryday https://t.co/hHOD5FpPRf
items.description: Video. A 2019 DHS '#WhyISeeSay / Protect Your Every Day' PSA. Ordinary people, including a woman on a city bus and a family outside a building, speak to camera about what is worth protecting (family, community), with on-screen 'WHY' text and a closing See/Say card. It is a narrated testimonial awareness spot. It predates the second Trump administration. | If you see something, why do you say something? I see safe from my friends. For much immunity. For everyone here, we all have something worth protecting, a why that unifies us. Reports of suspicious activity to local authorities. If you see something, say something. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: With @NASCAR, we’re working together to identify and report suspicious activity, so everyone stays safe at the Pennzoil 400 in Las Vegas. If you see something, say something. #SeeSay #ProtectYourEveryDay https://t.co/TtMvvb2Jia
items.description: Video. A 2019 DHS and NASCAR 'See Something, Say Something' PSA. Driver Kurt Busch stands in his racing suit and speaks directly to camera, telling fans at the track that safety is everyone's responsibility and to report suspicious activity. It is a static narrated spokesperson spot with NASCAR and DHS logos. It predates the second Trump administration. | Hi, I'm Kurt Bush. Safety and security is everyone's responsibility. While you're at the track, if you see something, say something. Report any suspicious activity to your local law enforcement agency. Thanks for your help and enjoy the race. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: By working with the @MLB to identify and report suspicious activity, you can make sure everyone is safe at the ballgame on #OpeningDay. #ProtectYourEveryDay #WhyISeeSay https://t.co/SzOboKBkge
items.description: Video. A 2019 DHS and MLB '#WhyISeeSay / Protect Your Every Day' Opening Day PSA. A woman outside a ballpark and fans tailgating speak to camera about protecting their team and community ('it's more than just a game'), closing with a See/Say card. It is a narrated testimonial awareness spot. It predates the second Trump administration. | If you see something, why do you say something? I see say for everyone here, for my team. Because it's more than just a game. We all have something worth protecting, a why that unifies us. Reports of suspicious activity to local authorities. If you see something, say something. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: With @NASCAR, we’re working together to identify and report suspicious activity, so everyone stays safe at the #Geico500 track at @TalladegaSuperS. #ProtectYourEveryDay #SeeSay https://t.co/GC0HLwXfvZ
items.description: Video. A 2019 DHS and NASCAR 'See Something, Say Something' PSA. Driver Chris Buescher (Kroger car) stands in his racing suit and speaks directly to camera, telling fans at the Talladega track that safety is everyone's responsibility and to report suspicious activity. It is a static narrated spokesperson spot with NASCAR and DHS logos. It predates the second Trump administration. | Hi, this is Chris Buscher. Safety and security is everyone's responsibility. While you're at the track, if you see something, say something. Report any suspicious activity to your local law enforcement agency. items.tweet_text: Did you know that @CISAgov is working behind the scenes, around the clock to protect this country’s critical infrastructure from physical and cyber threats? @DHS_Wolf outlines the incredible work that these men and women do every day to keep us safe. https://t.co/kWKiwqamgY
items.description: Video. Acting DHS Secretary Chad Wolf delivers a direct-to-camera address in a studio (US flag, CISA seal on screen) outlining CISA's COVID-19 critical-infrastructure and cybersecurity work, with brief B-roll of a call-center worker. It is an institutional informational message driven by continuous speech, not a music track. | to the dedicated professionals of DHS. As you know, this department is utilizing each component to combat the COVID-19 outbreak. Today, I'd like to talk to you about the unique efforts that the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has contributed to our shared mission. Under the leadership of Director Chris Krebs, CISIS serves as a nation's risk advisor coordinating with our interagency, state, local, and private sector partners to spread awareness of the pandemic's impact on our critical infrastructure. One of CISIS's most important contributions has been its guidance on the essential critical infrastructure workforce. This guidance is a valuable resource for state and local partners as they make decisions regarding essential services and how to keep them up and running during stay at home orders. items.description: A 2022 CBP video about the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act: a narrated voiceover reads the legal provisions while full-screen text cards appear over b-roll of ports, cargo ships, trucks at a border crossing, and the CBP.gov website. It consists of narration plus text slides with no music track. | Forced labor is an egregious human rights abuse that traps approximately 25 million people around the world in violent unjust and abusive working conditions. It hurts vulnerable workers, undermines the competitiveness of US businesses, and exposes American consumers to purchasing unethically sourced goods. US federal law prohibits the importation of merchandise, mined, produced, or manufactured wholly or in part by Forced Labor. The Weger Forced Labor Prevention Act reinforces this prohibition of goods made with Forced Labor established in the terror back of 1930. items.description: Video in which HSI's Robert Lombardi speaks to camera in front of a Cyber Crimes Center (C3) backdrop, telling parents that online predators target children over the holidays and directing viewers to ice.gov/sextortion. It is a single speaker with captions and no music track. | I'm Robert Lombardi with Homeland Security Investigations, Child Exploitation and Investigations Unit. I want to remind parents that online predators are praying on our unsuspective children more than ever. Despite our guidance to kids not to talk to strangers, our kids are often doing exactly that right under our noses, in our living rooms, in the back seats of our cars, in the classrooms and more using mobile devices. Never before have our children been so vulnerable. And this is especially a concern over the holidays when our kids have more time on their hands. And criminals know it. items.tweet_text: Tis the season for shopping and staying safe online. Scammers look to your personal and financial info to make their season bright. Protect yourself and your family before shopping online with these tips from the team at @CISAgov. ⬇️ #12DaysofTips https://t.co/TAqq4gUnwz
items.description: A holiday cyber-safety video in which a CISA spokesperson wearing a Christmas sweater speaks to camera in front of a CISA step-and-repeat backdrop, advising viewers to use multi-factor authentication, shop trusted sources, and avoid phishing, ending at cisa.gov/shopsafely. It is a single speaker in a static setting, consisting of speech with no music track. | Happy Holidays! Sissa wants everyone to enjoy the holiday season, but we know that while you're breaking out your ugly sweater, bad actors are trying to steal your joy, your identity, and your money. How can you stop these scrooches in their tracks? First, always ensure you have multi-factor authentication turned on. Passwords can be hacked, so add one more level of security, your fingerprint, your face, something only you have. Second, shop through trusted sources, and watch out for fishing emails. Never give your account info out via text for email. Finally, if your password is still 12345, you're getting a hole in your stock. Learn more at sissa.gov slash shop safely. Happy Holidays! | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text:
According to U.S. Department of Homeland Security Blue Campaign, violent kidnapping is not the most prevalent way traffickers claim victims. Listen in to Forensic Interview Specialist Lauren G. and learn more. ⬇️ 
https://www.dhs.gov/blue-campaign/myths-and-misconceptions https://t.co/ka4h3EhyPB
items.description: An audiogram from the DHS Blue Campaign '#TacklingTrafficking' series: a static blue graphic with a play icon and audio-waveform animation plays a recorded clip of Forensic Interview Specialist Lauren G. saying that trafficking victims are typically groomed rather than kidnapped, with her words shown as text-card captions. There is no video footage and no music, only narrated interview audio over a fixed graphic. | Unlike what is portrayed in the media, trafficking victims are groomed by the trafficker and not necessarily randomly kidnapped. It is not out of the realm of possibility, however, and there have been known cases of individuals being kidnapped because they began to uncover the trafficker's scheme and decide they no longer wanted to be a part of it, so they are taken by force and held against their will. But that typically happens after the victim has been in the situation for some time. So this is another myth which has been around for many years as it was the thing to look for when kidnappings first started making way into the lives of so many families here in the United States. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tag

items.tweet_text: Kelbie aims to leave a lasting legacy as a National Tribal Affairs Advocate with @FEMA, inspiring future leaders to keep the needs of tribal nations at the forefront. She hopes her work will be remembered for elevating the importance of our Native American communities in the #DHSmission. #NativeAmericanHeritageMonth
items.description: A talking-head employee profile for National Native American Heritage Month: Kelbie, a FEMA National Tribal Affairs Advocate, speaks to camera in a FEMA operations center with subtitles, describing how she would like to be remembered by tribal nations. It is a single-subject interview with a title card and no music. | I would like to be remembered as someone who did the most amount of good, for the most amount of tribes, for the most amount of time. I really like that particular saying, I want to be remembered as someone who helped push other people to do better, that for years after I'm out of this position, they're still thinking, you know, first and foremost, what about tribes, and that I'm continuing to leave a legacy of positive impact that people will pick up and continue into their rest of their careers in building allies wherever they're at for tribal nations. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text:
🎁 This holiday season, shop smart and stay safe! Beware of counterfeit goods that may pose safety risks. @CBP warns that fake products—like electronics, toys, and cosmetics—can be dangerous. Always buy from trusted retailers because fake goods can lead to real dangers. ⬇️ 
https://www.cbp.gov/trade/fakegoodsrealdangers
items.description: A nearly two-minute flat 2D animated explainer about counterfeit goods for holiday shoppers, narrated throughout by an instructional voiceover (online shoppers, a shuttered 'OUT OF BUSINESS / CLOSED FOREVER' store, a burning phone, hammer-and-chains imagery) and closing on the CBP logo with a QR code. It uses cartoon styling and is narrated consumer-safety instruction. | We all buy stuff online. It's often quick, easy, and cheap. But is it always safe? In the US, we import over a billion small packages every year. And many contain fake goods that can pose real dangers. Like baby formula or cosmetics made with unknown ingredients, counterfeit prescription medications containing harmful chemicals, toys and crafts made with lead paint or other environmentally hazardous materials, faulty counterfeit car parts, bogus electronics that can catch fire. The list goes on and on. Not only can fake goods pose serious health and safety risks to you and your family, they also waste your hard-earned money, contribute to loss of American jobs, and support criminal activity like human trafficking or forced labor. US Customs and Border Protection is looking out for the American consumer. Before good

ICE special agents ask your assistance to identify victims of a South Carolina childcare worker turned private babysitter in an ongoing child sexual exploitation and sextortion investigation. Details and reporting info: https://go.dhs.gov/wi6

items.description: Video. A Know2Protect PSA on online child sexual exploitation built from talking-head interviews with ICE special agents (Steven Moran, Ben Miller) plus title graphics and a closing URL card. It consists of interview testimony, with no music track. | The threat of child online exploitation has never been bigger. In the 20 years I've been working, I've never seen this many leads come in. We see that taking different forms, but essentially it's when an adult offender is targeting a juvenile in the online or digital environment with the ultimate goal of some sort of sexual victimization. People don't know that this crime is happening at such an alarming rate because it is uncomfortable to talk about. Bringing it to the forefront can help prevent the crime from happening in the first place. One of the things that we always want parents to understand is predators go where the kids are. In the past playgrounds, parks, public places, that's where offenders would go. Now, the digital environment is the playground for these kids. The Notaprotect campaign will educate and empower children, teens, parents, trusted adults and policymakers to prevent and combat online child sexual exploitation

Last year we had 147 unduplicated students at the Workforce Center, this year we have 198. A new marketing company study for higher education finds trade school enrollment is expected a rise by 6% over the next 5 years. Local trade school administrators say there are multiple reasons for the increase. One year certificate or two-year degree they can go straight into the workforce and be making ahead of household wages. Administrators at John Woods Workforce Development Program say whereas once parents were wanting their kids to get a four-year degree financially it may not be their best option. And this is just as bad. So take me to the beginning. What did you hear first? What are they telling you? What did you think? items.tweet_text: Anti-ICE rhetoric from elected officials puts everyone at risk. https://t.co/Xi8hpvUdmh
items.description: Video. A Newsmax remote interview with ICE Deputy Director Madison Sheehan saying that anti-ICE rhetoric from elected officials endangers agents, with b-roll of Dallas police vehicles. It is a televised news interview. | What does that sort of rhetoric mean for the agents who are working in the department? Well, let me be very clear, the job of the men and women of ISIS to enforce immigration law as it's written. Our job is not to pick winners and losers. We go out and enforce the laws that are on the books. If these lawmakers want to criticize ICE for their work, they should consider changing the law which they fully have the power to do. But President Trump and Secretary Nome empower the men and women of ICE to make sure that we are enforcing the law as it's written, securing our border and defending the homeland every single day. And I'll also say that the men and women of ICE have clear placards on their body armor. They wear their badges. They, you know, when you are interacting with an ICE officer, and that's standard to set very high with the scrutiny as well as the training that every ICE officer goes through.

AMERICAN WORKERS FIRST! 

@SecretaryLCD: Through Project Firewall investigations, we’re “making sure these companies are…advertising to the American Worker FIRST” 🔥 https://t.co/bjD3D2uTCi
items.description: A Newsmax LIVE remote interview with Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer speaking about the Project Firewall enforcement initiative and H-1B and visa matters, with Newsmax chyrons ('LABOR DEPT. INVESTIGATES VISA ABUSE'). | There shouldn't be any confusion about how important this initiative is. It's an enforcement initiative. Project Firewall is to protect the American worker. This administration has been very clear about looking through the lens of the American worker first. So, it was very important to me and the Labor Department that really for the first time in America's history, the Secretary has not signed personally or used the tool to crack down on these investigations. And when we're protecting the American worker, not only outside of the H1B program, but inside the H1B visa program as well. So I can understand that there's been some conversation about that. What we want to do first and foremost is making sure that these companies are, first of all, advertising to the American worker first. And that is, first and foremost, what should happen.

It's federal law, which requires us to lock up criminal legal aliens, hold them without bond and put them in immigration proceedings. And you know, Operation Angel Honor, which was for Lincoln Riley and her family, that just shows the impact that ICE makes every day across the country.

Breaking ice to keep America moving.

Winter weather doesn’t stop commerce, or the U.S. Coast Guard. 

In 2025, @USCG facilitated the movement of $5.4T in maritime commerce and 1.8B tons of cargo across U.S. waterways. From the Northeast to the Great Lakes, our icebreaking crews ensure critical supplies reach communities, even in the harshest winter conditions. With historic funding from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the Coast Guard is recapitalizing our domestic icebreaker fleet and maximizing our return on investment across America’s waterways.

items.tweet_text: The only thing standing between Americans and a wide open border is President @realDonaldTrump and the members of Congress who stand with @DHSgov. https://t.co/yRULzg0rnK
items.description: Video. A White House and broadcast clip shows President Trump delivering his State of the Union address from the House rostrum, saying that only he and congressional Republicans stand between Americans and an open border. A lower-third shows a number to text 'SOTU' for updates. It is a televised speech with no music or added editing effects. | We can never forget that many in this room not only allowed the border invasion to happen before I got involved, but indeed they would do it all over again if they ever had the chance. If they ever got elected, they would open up those borders to some of the worst criminals anywhere in the world. The only thing standing between Americans and a wide open border right now is President Donald J. Trump and our great Republican patriots in Congress. Thank you, thank you.

Read how one CBP officer made an impact on mental wellness with K9s and is the agency's only hostage/crisis negotiator for the @FBI. Check out this month's Frontline Magazine.

items.description: A CBP officer (Monica Williams) introduces her crisis-response and wellness K9 'Izzy' in a subtitled talking-head testimonial, partly at a port of entry and partly in front of DHS and CBP flags. The tweet includes the text 'Find your purpose with us'. The video is a spoken testimonial. No music track. | My name is Monica Williams and this is Izzy. As first responders, we're exposed to so much and unfortunately we internalize a lot of that. It is very important to be able to help our workforce by promoting mental wellness. And not only do we help our employees but we also help their families and the communities that we serve. In my 27 years in this career, I am the only CVP crisis hostage negotiator and trainer for the FBI. Find out more about what Izzy and I do by reading the latest edition of the Frontline magazine.

items.description: Captioned interview and b-roll recap of National Police Week memorial events (honor guards, bagpipers, agents bowing heads) with spoken soundbites. There are a number of other agencies that come together and represent the police law enforcement community as a whole. We remember all of the officers who have passed in the line of duty and have gave the ultimate sacrifice. I take a great deal of pride in being able to honor these folks. It means a lot to me and it's something that I hold very dear.

CBP is holding the line for FIFA World Cup 2026!  CBP Officers stationed across America and around the world stand ready to process international travelers swiftly so everyone can enjoy the games.

We’ll also be making sure counterfeit merchandise is stopped, no one wants a fake jersey!

📸: @SecMullinDHS
items.description: Selfie-style talking-head video of a DHS official holding a World Cup soccer ball in an office, with caption text, speaking about CBP readiness for FIFA 2026. No music track. | Alright guys, I'm not going to sit here and pretend like I'm a big soccer fan because I am not. I'm going to sit here and brag about these different agencies. CBP, which is our custom board of protection, is going to be responsible for processing five to seven million people in a very short period of time. Now think about that. They're not just going to be processing you. They're also going to be looking for counterfeit tickets and counterfeit merchandise. All to make sure over a 39-day period in 78 matches is going to go off without a hitch.

items.description: A 3.5-minute single-camera recording of HUD Secretary Scott Turner delivering budget testimony before a Congressional committee, with his 'Hon. A group of DC-based journalists, the White House Correspondents' Association, has long dictated which journalists get to ask questions of the President of the United States.

Not anymore.

Today, I was proud to announce that we are giving the power back to the people.

Moving forward, the ‘White House Press Pool,’ will be determined by the White House Press Team. 

Legacy outlets who have participated in the press pool for decades will still be allowed to join – but we will also be offering the privilege to well-deserving outlets who have never been allowed to share in this awesome responsibility.

🚨 @POTUS is taking executive action to protect fans from exploitative ticket scalping and bring commonsense reforms to live entertainment.

The Order directs the Federal Trade Commission to:

— Work with the Attorney General to ensure that competition laws are appropriately enforced in the concert and entertainment industry.

— Rigorously enforce the Better Online Ticket Sales (BOTS) Act and promote its enforcement by state consumer protection authorities.

— Ensure price transparency at all stages of the ticket-purchase process, including the secondary ticketing market.

— Evaluate and, if appropriate, take enforcement action to prevent unfair, deceptive, and anti-competitive conduct in the secondary ticketing market.

— The Order directs the Secretary of the Treasury and Attorney General to ensure that ticket scalpers are operating in full compliance with the Internal Revenue Code and other applicable law.

— Treasury, the Department of Justice, and the FTC will also deliver a report within 180 days summarizing actions taken to address the issue of unfair practices in the live concert and entertainment industry and recommend additional regulations or legislation needed to protect consumers in this industry.

President Trump’s message has been simple and consistent from the beginning:

To countries around the world — bring us your best offers, and President Trump will listen.

Deals will only be made if they benefit American workers and address our Nation’s crippling trade deficits.

America does not need other countries as much as other countries need us.

President Trump knows this.

He’s going to use the leverage of our market and our country to the advantage of the people he represents.

On the other hand, countries like China who retaliate and try to double down on their mistreatment of America are making a gigantic mistake.

President Trump has a spine of steel.

America will not bend, and we will not break under his leadership.

President Trump is guided by a firm belief that America must be able to produce essential goods for our own people and export them to the rest of the world.

A bold step forward for America and the U.S. Coast Guard.  

On August 10, we’ll commission the Storis (WAGB 21), our first polar icebreaker in 25+ years. This historic milestone strengthens U.S. Arctic presence, protects national security, and continues America’s leadership in the region.

The Storis is a game-changer for Arctic security, and will bolster the Coast Guard’s ability to control, secure, and defend the U.S. border around Alaska and maritime approaches in the Arctic.

Follow us for updates & an inside look at this historic milestone! #uscg #forcedesign2028 #arctic 
@USCGArctic @DHSgov @Sec_Noem

It's the latest federal probe into allegations of financial wrongdoing this one by the U.S. Department of Labor. The Secretary of Labor, writing in a letter sent to the Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development, quote, I am appalled at what we are hearing about potential fraud coming from numerous benefits programs in Minnesota. Alongside @DeptofWar, @USCG conducted a boarding and seizure of the Motor Tanker Bella I this morning in the North Atlantic. Following a sustained shadowing effort across the Atlantic by Coast Guard Cutter Munro, tactical Coast Guard teams leveraged our powerful maritime law enforcement authorities to secure Bella I through a tightly executed joint operation.
 
Through a whole of government effort and seamless coordination, our maritime fighting force is proud to own the sea, uphold international law, and defend America.

#USCG #WeOwnTheSea @DHSgov

This morning, a @USCG tactical team, supported by @USMC and @USNavy , boarded and seized Motor Tanker (M/T) Olina in international waters east of the Caribbean. Interagency coordination, and an unstoppable joint force, were instrumental in executing a safe, carefully orchestrated operation consistent with international law.
 
Powered by unique law enforcement authorities and specialized capabilities, the Coast Guard is seizing sanctioned oil tankers and protecting the American people from threats on the high seas. M/T Olina is the latest example.
 
Bravo Zulu to our maritime fighting force – and our partners at @DeptofWar and @StateDept – for their relentless execution of this mission. The Coast Guard continues operations to control, secure, and defend U.S. borders and maritime approaches – where defense of America begins.
 
#USCG #WeOwnTheSea

What the media won't tell you is that after ICE detained the father, our officers spent time with the young boy — even taking him through a drive-through for some food — before reuniting him with his father.
 
The smears against our officers and this agency are relentless and continue to put our personnel at greater risk of attack. It must end.

On January 21, ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) responded to a request from the Sherburne County Sheriff’s Office in Zimmerman, MN, to help locate a missing 7-year-old girl after an AMBER Alert. HSI teams braved sub-freezing temperatures, canvassed neighborhoods, and worked closely with local law enforcement, gathering surveillance information to aid the search.
 
On January 22, HSI was notified that the child was found safe and the alleged sexual assaulter and kidnapper, 28-year-old Joseph Andrew Bragg, was taken into custody.
 
HSI is proud to have helped bring this young girl home and ensure alleged child predators are removed from Minnesota’s streets.

The SAVE America Act is overwhelmingly popular with all Americans because each provision is rooted in common sense.

The SAVE America Act has five simple requirements:

Number one, voters have to show ID to cast a ballot in an American election. 90% of Americans – including ~80% of Democrat voters – agree with this.

Number two, the SAVE America Act will require all voters to show proof of citizenship in order to register to vote.

Number three, the SAVE America Act abolishes the incredibly unsecure practice of universal mail-in ballots which throw the door wide open for fraud. Importantly, the SAVE America Act maintains exceptions for Americans to use mail-in-ballots for illness, disability, military, or travel reasons. 
Number four, the SAVE America Act permanently bans men from competing in women’s sports. 
Number five, the SAVE America Act bans transgender mutilation surgery for children.

Passing the SAVE America Act is the most important thing that Republicans can do right now to strengthen election integrity.

This officer’s extraordinary bravery embodies the selfless service of DHS law enforcement.

Our ICE officers and agents are HEROES.

On March 25, 2026, an ICE agent helping to support @TSA operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York jumped into action to help save the life of a one-year-old child experiencing a medical emergency.

The heroic actions of this officer began when a one-year-old child became unresponsive in the arms of his father, unable to breathe for almost two minutes. CCTV review shows a passenger in a TSA Precheck line holding his one-year-old in his arms when the child’s arms go lifeless; panic ensues, and the father is seen scrambling around the area, and calling for help.  

The agent working at his post, heard the screams from the father and other passengers and sprinted to the scene. The father handed the child to the officer, who then assessed the unresponsive child and began performing the Heimlich maneuver. After a few seconds, the child started breathing again. EMS personnel arrived on scene with medical equipment to further monitor and re-assess the child. The child was re-assessed and determined to be healthy enough to fly.

Nine U.S. citizens and illegal aliens, including two John Does, were charged in a federal crackdown on benefit fraud schemes in Massachusetts by ICE @HSINewEngland and its partners.

The accused allegedly used stolen identities belonging to U.S. citizens from Puerto Rico to steal more than $1.1 million in taxpayer-funded programs — including SNAP, MassHealth and Social Security benefits.

Stolen IDs were first used to obtain government-issued identification, including Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles credentials and, in some instances, U.S. passports, which were then used to apply for and receive public benefits.
items.description: Horizontal video. We will continue every day in this fight until we bring those responsible to justice.

An Ohio man who led police on an hours-long chase in 2024 was sentenced to 30 years in prison March 24 for child sexual abuse crimes following an ICE HSI Detroit probe.

Johnathan Brown, 34, secretly recorded young girls, hiding outside bedroom windows and placing cameras inside a laundry basket to record minors after they exited showers. 

Brown also groomed a teenager, beginning when she was 15, eventually filming himself having sex with the victim. 

Special thanks to the Butler Township Police Department, Miami Valley Human Trafficking Task Force and @OSHP.

He had outside bedroom windows and put cameras and laundry baskets to record minors getting out of the shower. He then told the victims that he needed the videos for quote medical reasons. Court records say that he also groomed a 15-year-old and sold sexually explicit pictures threatening self-harm to get that teen to cooperate. In August of 2024, he led police on a wild chase around Dayton before driving onto a moving train and starting the SWAT situation. —Sexual performance of a child under 14, 1st degree felony: 99 years
—Possession of CSAM/video, 2nd degree felony: 20 years

items.tweet_text: .@POTUS: "Honoring the British King might seem an ironic beginning to our celebration of 250 years of American independence — but in fact, no tribute could be more appropriate. Long before Americans had a nation or Constitution, we first had a culture, a character, and a creed. Before we ever proclaimed our independence, Americans carried within us the rarest of gifts: moral courage, and it came from a small but mighty kingdom from across the sea."

items.description: NBC News Now sit-down interview of Secretary Rubio (US flag behind, NBC logo) discussing the Straits of Hormuz and a UN resolution on Iran. Static interview shot with reporter, continuous talking, no music. | Did President Trump raise the issue of Iran with China? He did, and it was important because the Chinese side said they are not in favor of militarizing the Straits of Hormuz, and they're not in favor of a tolling system. And that's our position. We will never support an Iranian tolling system in the Straits of Hormuz, nor do we think they have a right to put minds in international waters. And so it's good that we have alliance, or at least agreement on that point. I think the fundamental question is what are we going to do about it? We have a resolution now before the United Nations, in which 100 and something countries have co-signed. The Bahrainis are the sponsor, but we're strongly behind it, and we've been pushing very hard on it. And it very clearly makes those points. So we hope the Chinese will vote for it. So right now we haven't gotten their commitment to vote for it yet at the United Nations. Maybe that'll change after today's meeting. I don't know. | Reviewed video

.@AFergusonFTC explains how the @WHFraudTF is using AI-driven technological solutions to stop fraudulent payments from leaving federal agencies:

items.description: FTC's Ferguson in a seated interview describing AI fraud-detection systems used by the White House Fraud Task Force. Sustained spoken transcript, no music. | So, all of the agencies are supposed to have anti-fraud prevention systems in place. The bi administration turned a lot of those off and let them languish. And what we were able to do basically, sort of like building on the doge effort, is work with these agencies with the data that they have, the data that other agencies have, and publicly available data, and build technological solutions, most of which are AI-driven that can take all of these data. And so when a claims payment request comes in, basically AI puts up a flag and says, very likely fraudulent. And all of the agencies have administrative authority to withhold those payments until they know that this is a real person that's actually qualifying for this request. If you have to do that by hand, if you have to have individuals go out and figure all these out, the money just goes out the door, and then you have to get the doge to chase it and they can't get it all back. items.tweet_text:
.@SecretaryBurgum at the Pikka development on the North Slope, says Alaska will play "a huge role going forward in the major shift in the geopolitics of energy."

"It is 8 days from Anchorage to Tokyo, and most of that is along the Aleutian Islands. That's all U.S.-controlled territorial waters... vs. right now, a country like Japan getting 92% of their oil from the Strait of Hormuz, and it can be a 30, 35-day trip on a good day—or maybe not at all."
items.description: Video. Interior Secretary Burgum at the Pikka development on Alaska's North Slope talking about energy dominance and shipping advantages versus the Strait of Hormuz. Talking-head remarks, no music. | When we talk about energy dominance, we do talk about having energy to sell to our friends and allies so they don't have to buy it from our adversaries, the ones that are waging war and waging terrorism. So, again, Alaska, not just lowering the prices for all Americans but playing a huge role going forward in the major shift in the geopolitics of energy in the world. It is eight days from Anchorage to Tokyo, and most of that is along the Aleutian Islands. That's all U.S. controlled territorial waters with the U.S. Navy. Versus right now, a country like Japan getting 92% of their oil from the straight to Harmoose, and it can be a 30-35-day trip on a good day or maybe not at all right now. | Direct keyframe + tweet-text review: an on-camera spoken-word clip (remarks/statement) featuring Secretary Burgum.

Wherever the American Soldier walks, wherever he fights... and wherever he falls, he does it for the destiny of a nation like no other... and for the fate of Freedom on this earth...

By their deaths, those who have gone before us in battle have redeemed the promise of our Founding for each future generation.

They've not just made the Ultimate Sacrifice, they have offered the Ultimate Proof that we Americans do indeed love Liberty. We do cherish the self-government given to us by our forefathers. We do believe with all our souls in the mission that God has given to America. And we do intend with all our strength and heart to hold high the torch our heroes handed to us—and we will never, ever let it fall."

The next evening, the San Juan Marine Unit launched a coordinated interdiction operation. Two Coastal Interceptor Vessels and multiple aircraft moved in, guided by constant vectors from our aircrews.

At 9:51 p.m., the targeted vessel was intercepted north of San Juan. The suspects tried to evade capture and began dumping contraband into the water. In a decisive moment, the AMO Black Hawk crew deployed Air Disabling Fire, stopping the vessel cold.

Three Dominican Republic nationals were taken into custody, and five bales containing 391 lbs. of cocaine were seized and transferred to the Homeland Security Task Force. This operation highlights our relentless commitment to securing America’s borders and keeping dangerous drugs off our streets. 

Check out the full video here: https://ow.ly/TVYb50Z5kFS#SecuringAmerica 

#AMO #BorderSecurity #Teamwork

items.tweet_text: We know of no threat to the public. If we learn of any cause for concern, we will take action and communicate immediately with the American public. https://t.co/oddf59jFSH
items.description: Video. A TV 'Exit Interview' clip of Secretary Mayorkas (talking head with a subtitle bar) discussing drone sightings over New Jersey and asking Congress to expand DHS authorities. It is a broadcast interview, with no music. | And let me restate what we've said previously. It's very important. We know of no threat to people's security. And if we learn of any cause for concern, we will take action and we will communicate immediately with the American public. There are, and there have been thousands and thousands of drones flown across the United States for years. All drones, recreational drones, law enforcement drones. I spoke with an expert yesterday who has recorded over his home in California over the past six years, more than 13,000 drone detections. And so this is actually not a new phenomenon. What we need in the federal government is we need our authorities to catch up with the development of drone activity over the last 10 years. And so we have asked Congress for not only an extension of our authorities, but an expansion of them. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.tweet_text: President Biden also created the Sáttítla Highlands National Monument, protecting over 224,000 acres of otherworldly and spectacular landscape in northern California. At the new monument’s core sits the Medicine Lake Volcano, a massive dormant volcano that has fostered a dramatic landscape dotted with cinder cones, volcanic craters, spatter cones, and hundreds of cave-like lava tubes. The Sáttítla Highlands include the ancestral homelands of and are sacred to the Pit River Tribe and Modoc Peoples. The monument will be managed by the Department of Agriculture’s U.S. Forest Service.

What do you get when you cross a previously convicted carjacker with a ghost gun? A FOOT PURSUIT, OF COURSE.

When you’ve just been released from a 3-year prison sentence for carjacking, you probably (definitely) shouldn’t be packing a firearm.

A #PremierSector agent saw a single CHP officer on a stop with two subjects and decided to stop and assist because teamwork makes the dream work. As our agent attempted to conduct a Terry frisk for officer safety, one subject decided he was going to test his 100-yard dash time and sprinted into an alfalfa field to get away. 

He must have thought the weapon and ammo he was carrying was invisible while he was tossing it into the field in front of our pursuing agent. Guess what? We saw it!! 👀

After taking the subject into custody, our agent turned him and his recovered ghost gun 👻🔫 back over to CHP. This felon must really miss prison cafeteria food because he’s working extra hard to go back. 

Video courtesy of David Abatti and @pinshi_metishi_760

#CBP #DHS #BorderPatrol #CHP #FelonFails

items.tweet_text: SPLASHDOWN IN TEXAS! On 5/27, smugglers tried to outsmart the U.S. Border Patrol with a bold move—floating a pickup truck loaded with suspicious bundles across the Rio Grande on a homemade raft. Once on U.S. soil, they made a break for it. But as agents closed in, the driver veered back and plunged the truck into the river in a desperate attempt to escape. Chaos followed as individuals scrambled in the water to retrieve the suspected narcotics—but USBP agents acted fast. They recovered 6 bundles of marijuana weighing nearly 250 lbs. Smugglers are getting bolder, but USBP always stands at the ready.

Maritime Safety and Security Team (MSST) Honolulu 91107 stands at the forefront of the Coast Guard’s mission to protect America’s interests.

Specializing in Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security, MSST Honolulu conducts high-risk vessel escorts, enforces safety and security zones, and executes maritime pursuit operations to prevent illegal activity. Applying our unique authorities and capabilities, they are at the leading edge of our operations to control, secure, and defend U.S. borders and maritime approaches.

MSST Honolulu’s presence underscores the Coast Guard’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific, strengthens regional stability, and plays a key role in advancing U.S. interests in a dynamic and strategic region.
#USCG #MSSTHonolulu #MaritimeSecurity #IndoPacific

A new chapter begins.

@Sec_Noem  unveiled Force Design 2028: a bold, once-in-a-generation plan to transform the 234-year-old Coast Guard into a modern, mission-ready force. 🇺🇸

Thank you, Secretary Noem, for your leadership and bold vision to transform the Coast Guard through Force Design 2028.

Through FD 2028, the Service is revolutionizing how it functions and operates to ensure decisive advantage over adversaries. Focused on four campaigns - People, Organization, Contracting and Acquisition, and Technology - FD 2028 is re-shaping the Coast Guard into a stronger, more ready and capable fighting force.

Coast Guard crews around the country work diligently to prevent illegal narcotics from entering the United States.

Coast Guard Cutter Kimball exemplified these operations during a recent patrol from February through April, during which they conducted multiple drug interdictions off the coasts of Mexico and Central and South America. This culminated in Kimball offloading more than $191 million worth of cocaine in April.

As the Coast Guard continues to surge assets across our southern border and maritime approaches, our crews have been leading the fight against drug cartels and Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCO). The dedicated efforts of Kimball – and men and women across the Coast Guard – are directly impacting the ability of cartels and TCOs to smuggle illicit drugs into our communities. 

📷PA3 Avery Tibbets & MST3 Austin Wiley

@DHSgov @USCGPACAREA @USCGHawaiiPac 

#USCG #USCGHawaii #IndoPacific #druginterdiction

items.tweet_text:
This is what generational change looks like. Yesterday, U.S. Coast Guard Cutter (USCGC) Storis transited the Panama Canal, marking a significant milestone on its maiden voyage towards its future homeport in Juneau.
 
After departing the Panama Canal, Storis met three recently decommissioned 110’ Island-Class Patrol Boats from Alaska – USCGCs Liberty, Mustang, and Naushon. These are the last of the storied 110’s, being succeeded by the modern Sentinel-class Fast Response Cutters.
 
Today’s passage exemplifies the Coast Guard’s transformation under Force Design 2028. As the United States’ third polar icebreaker, Storis will bring innovative capabilities and crewing to assure access to the polar regions and protect U.S. sovereignty. As the Service modernizes its fleet and infrastructure, Storis will continue the return on America’s investment in the Coast Guard. @USCGPACAREA @USCGAlaska @DHSgov 

#USCG #Storis #PolarOperations #PanamaCanal #ForceDesign2028 #ArcticPresence #IcebreakerFleet

Today marks the beginning of a new chapter for @USCG. A nearly $25 billion investment will transform the Service through modernization of assets, infrastructure, and technology. This funding supports Force Design 2028, Secretary Noem’s comprehensive effort to modernize operations and capabilities to ensure the Coast Guard remains the finest maritime fighting force ready to protect and defend the American people for decades to come.  
 
We extend our deep appreciation for the leadership of the Administration, including @POTUS  and @Sec_Noem, and leaders in Congress for recognizing the strategic importance of a ready, modern, and resilient Coast Guard.

Always ready, the men and women of the Coast Guard remain on watch across our maritime borders and approaches, where defense of America begins.

#USCG #ForceDesign2028 #ValuetoNation #EveryWarEveryShore
@DHSgov

Value to Nation: Across the Coast Guard’s range of missions, our men and women are dedicated to keeping Americans safe and delivering on the Nation’s historic investment in the Service. We continue to surge resources to control, secure, and defend 31,000 miles of U.S. maritime borders — where defense of America begins.

We are combating foreign terrorist organizations, cartels, and transnational organized crime.

We facilitate commerce vital to economic security and strategic mobility.

We are always ready to respond to a crisis or contingency that may come with little or no warning.

Continuing our transformation through Force Design 2028, the Coast Guard remains focused on maximizing value to the Nation through the most agile, capable, and responsive maritime fighting force.

#USCG #CoastGuard #ValueToNation #SemperParatus #ForceDesign2028 @DHSgov

A major milestone this week in the Coast Guard’s drug interdiction efforts: Since January 20, we’ve seized over 242,000 pounds of cocaine. With as little as 1.2g being enough to kill someone, that’s 91 million potentially lethal doses.  

@USCG continues to surge forces along the southern border and maritime approaches. The strategy is working. Applying our unique authorities and capabilities, we’ve stopped over 100% percent more cocaine than we did in 2024.

Bravo Zulu to the men and women of the Coast Guard. Through their tireless efforts – and close coordination with interagency partners – we are seizing record amounts of illegal drugs and making America safer. 
 
Read more: https://www.dhs.gov/news/2025/07/15/coast-guard-seizes-over-240000-pounds-cocaine-doubling-amount-interdicted-over

#USCG #druginterdiction #ValueToNation @DHSgov

Yesterday, @USCG commissioned the Fast Response Cutter Earl Cunningham, honoring Boatswain’s Mate Second Class Earl Cunningham, who gave his life in 1936 during a heroic rescue on Lake Michigan.

Cunningham’s courage and legacy now inspire the mission of this cutter, which will strengthen our capabilities to defend Alaska’s maritime border and respond to crises. Through historic investment in the Coast Guard, we have ordered additional Fast Response Cutters.

Welcome aboard, USCGC Earl Cunningham!  

Follow @USCGArctic for more news about the Cunningham and its crew.

Read more and hear from the CO here: https://www.mycg.uscg.mil/News/Article/4271141/if-not-us-who-a-conversation-with-the-co-of-our-newest-fast-response-cutter/

The Arctic demands access, power, and vigilance. @USCG delivers.

Through sustained efforts like Operation Frontier Sentinel, Coast Guard crews are protecting U.S. sovereignty, enhancing national security, and countering foreign malign influence in the Arctic. Following acquisition of Coast Guard Cutter Storis – the nation’s 1st icebreaker in over 25 years – we're bolstering our Arctic fleet through $7.8B+ in One Big Beautiful Bill funding for new icebreakers.

Continuing our return on America’s historic investment, the Coast Guard is ensuring access, controlling U.S. maritime borders and approaches, and delivering the operational advantage in the Arctic.

#USCG #Arctic #Polar #IceOperations @DHSgov @USCGArctic

Being Always Ready depends on every crew member. Become part of the Semper Paratus legacy. Join the Coast Guard ➡️ http://GoCoastGuard.com

Behind every successful patrol is a crew that keeps the cutter operational.

Aboard @USCG Cutter Stone, Machinery Technicians keep propulsion, power, and critical systems operating to ensure the cutter remains ready to operate and respond. Through Operation Pacific Viper, CGC Stone and other @USCG units have interdicted over 170K pounds of cocaine since early August. That took a total team effort. As a Machinery Technician, Smallboat Engineer, and Boarding Team Member, Petty Officer Fair ensured CGC Stone was always ready to operate and deliver results wherever the mission took the crew.

What can you bring to being Semper Paratus? Find out at http://GoCoastGuard.com

#USCG #MemberHighlight #SemperParatus @DHSgov @USCGPACAREA @USCGLANTAREA

Through Force Design 2028, the Coast Guard is delivering unprecedented return on America’s investment.

Over the past year, the Coast Guard seized 554,.000 pounds of illegal narcotics, interdicted 11,173 illegal aliens, saved 4,946 lives, saved or assisted over $974 million in property, and ensured the safe movement of 1.8 billion tons of maritime cargo — measurable outcomes across border control, flow of commerce, and contingency response.

As U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Polar Star began icebreaking operations for Operation Deep Freeze 2026, the cutter marked 50 years of service by breaking through Antarctic pack ice to ensure safe navigation and sustain U.S. operations in the polar regions. When the cruise ship Scenic Eclipse II became beset in Antarctic pack ice, Polar Star responded immediately, breaking it free and escorting it to open water — underscoring the importance of a robust U.S. icebreaker fleet.

America’s only heavy icebreaker continues to deliver where no other ship can operate.

#USCG #Icebreaking #PolarStar @USCGPACAREA @DHSgov

items.tweet_text:
Icebreaking is about precision. Every operation in frozen waterways is deliberate—driven by timing, judgment, and coordination in some of the most demanding operating conditions. From the Great Lakes to the Northeast to the Mid-Atlantic, @USCG crews continuously assess ice behavior, vessel movement, and environmental factors to ensure safe, reliable access where it’s needed most. As we modernize our domestic icebreaker fleet, we continue to facilitate commerce in response to ice impacts to navigation on our waterways. 

Read more here: https://www.dhs.gov/news/2026/02/04/coast-guard-responds-severe-winter-conditions-icebreaking-operations-eastern-united 

#USCG #Icebreaking #MTS #Commerce @DHSgov @USCGGreatLakes @USCGLANTAREA @USCGNortheast 

Clip credits in Instagram

items.tweet_text:
Carving a path through the Antarctic ice.

#USCG Cutter Polar Star is on station for Operation Deep Freeze, clearing the way for vital resupply ships to reach McMurdo Station.

Ever wonder how we navigate the ice so efficiently? The Coast Guard is accelerating our use of advanced robotic and autonomous systems, like the SkyDio X10D, to survey ice conditions, enhancing safety, vigilance, and mission effectiveness.

In some of the world’s most challenging environments, like the Antarctic, we’re unifying vigilance and innovation to empower our crews and secure U.S. interests.

@DHSgov @USCGPACAREA 

#SemperParatus

Relentless vigilance. Unifying leadership. Coordinated response.

In response to catastrophic flooding in Oahu, @USCG and @USNavy aircrews rescued seven people and one dog in separate incidents yesterday in Waialua and Yokohama Bay.

Alongside our federal, state, and local partners, the Coast Guard is bringing every capability to bear - cutters, boats, aircraft, and crisis leaders - as this response evolves.

As America’s maritime first responder, the Coast Guard stands with the people of Oahu.

Read more here: https://www.news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases/Article/4440335/coast-guard-partners-rescue-7-people-1-dog-during-flash-floods-on-oahu/

#USCG #SemperParatus #SoOthersMayLive

How did #USCG Cutter Polar Star celebrate its 50th birthday? By breaking a cruise ship free from Antarctic ice.

This was just one moment in the successful 55-day Operation Deep Freeze. The Polar Star’s crew also carved a 7-mile channel, enabling the delivery of millions of gallons of fuel and a new pier for the U.S. Antarctic Program. As the United States' only heavy polar icebreaker, the Polar Star's performance underscores its indispensable role in maintaining strategic year-round access to the polar regions. This is global impact – facilitating commerce and defending America’s national interests in these critical and challenging environments.

After 14,000 miles, the crew is heading home. Bravo Zulu on a historic deployment!

Read more: https://www.news.uscg.mil/Press-Releases/Article/4431373/us-coast-guard-cutter-polar-star-completes-operation-deep-freeze-2026-mission-d/

items.tweet_text:
LATEST CONSPIRATOR SENTENCED IN 13-YEAR ICE HSI ILLICIT SOFTWARE PROBE

A Florida woman got 22 months in prison and a $50,000 fine March 2 for trafficking illicit certificate of authenticity labels that bear Microsoft software activation codes.

Heidi Richards was sentenced in a 13-year, nationwide ICE @HSIKansasCity-led probe into a trafficking network that collectively harvested and resold at a discount over 600,000 illicit key codes worth over $900 million.

The labels and codes made counterfeit software appear legitimate.

The investigation so far includes $20.6 million in seized assets, as well as arrests, indictments and convictions of nine major distributors. DOJ calls this the largest software prosecution in its history.

Established on May 28, 1924, the USBP was born from a critical need to secure our expanding borders.

From its early days, with agents often providing their own horses and navigating vast, rugged terrains, the Border Patrol's mission has continuously evolved. Through eras of Prohibition, shifting immigration policies, and the complexities of national security, agents have adapted, utilizing new technologies and strategies to meet the challenges of their time. This rich history is a testament to a century of unwavering dedication and resilience.

Today, that legacy lives on through the brave men and women who stand guard 24/7. Their commitment ensures the integrity of our borders and the safety of our communities. As we reflect on 102 years of service, we honor every agent who has contributed to this vital mission. Happy 102nd Birthday, U.S. Border Patrol!

#USBP #BorderPatrol #NationalSecurity #HistoryOfService #Anniversary

items.tweet_text:
🚨ICYMI - 240 LIVES SAVED DURING ILLEGAL MARITIME MIGRATION ATTEMPT! 

On May 31, a Jacksonville Air and Marine Branch Multi-Role Enforcement Aircraft detected a surface target of interest about 65 nautical miles south of the Turks and Caicos Islands (TCI).

Air Interdiction Agents relayed information to TCI authorities and OPBAT partners, providing updated position, course, and speed reports.

The AMO aircrew conducted a successful over-the-air handoff of the STOI to a U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) aircraft.

USCG aircrew reported the vessel had lost one engine, was slowly taking on water, and occupants were observed bailing 3–5 gallons of water per minute.

At approximately 9:00 pm, USCG reported the vessel was dead in the water and occupants continued to bail water using buckets.

TCI authorities declared a search and rescue case due to increased risk of capsizing and launched four maritime surface assets. 

At approximately 1:00 a.m. on June 1, TCI authorities successfully rescued/interdicted the STOI.

TCI authorities reported a total of 240 migrants onboard: 191 adult males, 44 adult females, and 5 minors.

The passengers and crew were taken by Turks and Caicos authorities and did not reach U.S. soil.

WATCH: Nighttime Interdiction Takes Down 3 Dominican Republic Nationals!

On June 9, at approximately 11:00 PM local time, a Caribbean Air and Marine Branch Multi-Role Enforcement Aircraft detected a Target of Interest—a 19-foot Yola-type vessel with one outboard engine, three people onboard, and no navigation lights—about 29 nautical miles north of Arecibo, Puerto Rico. The suspicious vessel was tracked and monitored through coordinated air and marine surveillance, with a NASOC DHC-8 aircrew also providing coverage surveillance.
 
The San Juan Marine Unit launched a Coastal Interceptor Vessel to intercept, guided by real-time updates from the Caribbean Air and Marine Operations Center. After persistent tracking, Marine Interdiction Agents intercepted the vessel north of Camuy, Puerto Rico. Three Dominican Republic nationals and electronic devices were seized and transferred to the Homeland Security Task Force for further processing. This operation underscores the vigilance and teamwork of our air and marine units in protecting our maritime borders! #BorderSecurity

🚨40 Illegal Aliens Interdicted Near Western Puerto Rico!
 
On June 6, at 12:28 a.m., the Caribbean Air and Marine Operations Center detected a target of interest west of Desecheo Island. CAMOC relayed the information to a National Air Security Operations Center DHC-8 aircrew, who located the 25 to 30 foot rustic vessel with multiple people onboard.
 
The vessel appeared disabled and unable to make way. The DHC-8 aircrew maintained surveillance and guided a U.S. Coast Guard cutter to the location. As the cutter approached, the vessel began moving toward Puerto Rico’s shoreline.
 
The USCG intercepted the vessel at around 2 a.m. Forty individuals were apprehended - 36 nationals from the Dominican Republic (34 adult males, 2 adult females), three Haitian nationals (all adult males), and one Uzbekistan national (adult male).
 
Incredible teamwork to stop this maritime attempt! AMO continues to work alongside federal, state, and international partners to disrupt smuggling operations and safeguard national security!

🚨 WATCH P-3 Leads High-Speed Pursuit: Marijuana Seized, Ecuadorian Smugglers Arrested 🚨

A Jacksonville P-3, on routine patrol in the Caribbean Sea’s source and transit zone, detected a fast-moving vessel on June 11. The crew visually identified a 3-engine Ecuadorian-style go-fast boat loaded with fuel barrels and large packages. The position and details were quickly relayed to Joint Interagency Task Force South and the USCG.

USCG assets—including a helicopter and Over-the-Horizon vessels—responded rapidly. After an overflight, the suspect vessel stopped, allowing USCG teams to gain positive control.

Result: 3,960 pounds of marijuana seized and 2 Ecuadorian suspects detained.

Outstanding teamwork and coordination between NASOC-JAX, JIATF-S, and the USCG! #ProtectingAmerica #CounterNarcotics

U.S. citizen and San Diego resident Isaac Jimenez pleaded guilty June 16 to his role in an alien smuggling conspiracy that held would-be migrants hostage in Mexico.

💰While Jimenez did not personally hold aliens captive, he confessed to collecting tens of thousands of dollars in ransom payments from family members following an ICE @HSISanDiego probe with its California Homeland Security Task Force partners.

In at least two cases — a father of four U.S. citizen children and a young woman from Tijuana — THE VICTIMS DISAPPEARED after their families made multiple ransom payments to secure their freedom.

As part of his guilty plea, Jimenez agreed to pay $24,500 to the family members of the missing migrants for funeral and related expenses and as restitution.

➡️Visit our newsroom for more details in this ongoing case.

At more than 22,000 artifacts, a recent ICE HSI antiquities seizure in Florida is among the largest in the agency’s history as @HSITampa investigates its smugglers with @HSI_HQ's Cultural Property, Art and Antiquities Division.

More than a dozen experts and top archaeological specialists helped HSI Tampa identify and authenticate the objects. Preliminary indications show some artifacts may be between 1,000 to 5,000 years old from countries across Europe, Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean.

Cultural property, art and antiquities smuggling is a global crime that enables criminals to profit from stolen history, launder money and fund terrorism.

Alibaba Group Holding Limited (Alibaba) — one of China’s largest companies — and its U.S.-based payment processor, AUS Merchant Services Inc. agreed to a $600M non-prosecution agreement July 1 to resolve allegations that they failed to prevent merchants from selling and importing illegal pharmaceuticals, controlled substances, listed chemicals and pill presses into the U.S. 

An ICE @HSI_HQ probe with its @HSTFNCC partners led to Alibaba’s admission that it failed to prevent merchants using its Alibaba(dot)com and AliExpress(dot)com platforms from making about 80,000 product sales, including List I and II chemicals, pharmaceuticals and pharmaceutical counterfeiting equipment.

Alibaba operates one of the world’s largest business-to-business online marketplaces. AUS is a subsidiary of Ant Group, which operates Alipay, one of the largest mobile and digital payment platforms in the world.

Alibaba agreed to pay a criminal monetary penalty of $125 million and to forfeit $200 million. AUS agreed to pay a criminal monetary penalty of $85 million and to forfeit $190 million. 

“This non-prosecution agreement, financial resolution and required compliance reforms makes clear that global e-commerce companies must build systems that prevent the sale and distribution of illegal products before they reach the United States and the U.S. banking system,” said ICE HSI Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon.
